title: Batched Mosaic: introduce default batching/caching profiles and quantization fallback adapter
author: Priya Desai
description:
Context: We routinely see mismatches between workload characteristics observed at runtime and the static batching/caching defaults shipped with new model profiles. For mid-sized conversational workloads this causes ~8-15% higher token cost due to suboptimal microbatch sizes and overly-conservative KV cache TTLs. The goal of this PR is threefold in service of automatic unit-econ improvements: 1) introduce a compact set of 'mosaic' default batching + cache presets tailored to common workload archetypes (conversational, assistant-long, search-short, and rerank); 2) add a light-weight quantization fallback adapter that transparently routes to a compatible quantized variant when a requested profile is unavailable or cost budget hits; 3) expose a small unit-econ telemetry hook used by Redwood Optimize to validate defaults and trigger safe auto-tuning.

Summary of changes: added a new presets package under runtime/config/presets called mosaic-presets; added adapter logic in runtime/router to select fallback quantized variants; introduced a minimal telemetry event (econ.profile.suggestion) wired into the rollout path; updated model catalog meta to include mosaic hints; added docs and unit tests.

Why this is different: previous PRs focused on either batching heuristics or quant profiles independently. This PR combines compact, workload-aware presets plus a 'graceful fallback' quant adapter so that customers get consistent cost/latency behavior without manual profile selection. The presets are intentionally conservative in latency-sensitive clusters (low-latency SLOs) and more aggressive in cost-optimized tiers.

Checklist:
- [x] Presets implemented and documented
- [x] Router + fallback adapter implemented
- [x] Unit tests for adapter selection and fallback
- [x] Integration tests covering conv/search workloads in perf-canary harness
- [x] Telemetry event wired and validated through QA cluster
- [x] Migration script for model-catalog metadata
- [x] Rollout plan and safe-guard: canary + staged percentage

Key implementation notes:
- mosaic-presets exposes four named presets: conv.default, assistant.long, search.short, rerank.tight. Each preset includes: target_microbatch_tokens, expected_sequence_distribution (summary string), kv_cache_ttl_ms, and batch_backpressure_threshold. These fields are intentionally coarse-grained strings/numbers to avoid brittle tuning.
- The quant-fallback-adapter uses a short compatibility matrix (architecture -> compatible quant variants). When a request specifies a specific quant_profile but it is not available or triggers a budget-enforced rejection, the adapter attempts two fallbacks in order: 1) an equivalent lower-precision quant variant (e.g., int8 -> int4) if supported by hardware; 2) a CPU-safe compressed runtime if GPU capacity is unavailable. Each fallback emits econ.profile.suggestion with suggestion_reason set to one of: unavailable, capacity, budget.
- The telemetry hook includes: preset_applied, fallback_taken (bool), observed_latency_ms, tokens_generated, cost_estimate_usd. Only aggregated counters are emitted for privacy and cost reasons.
- Migration: model-catalog entries without a mosaic hint will default to conv.default for models whose seq_length_mean < 256, assistant.long otherwise.

Performance and safety:
- Canary results (perf-canary cluster): conv.default yields -11.8% token cost vs existing default at 95th p95 stable latency +/- 5ms; assistant.long shows -18% cost on long-context workloads with p95 +12ms mean delta (within SLO for dedicated capacity); search.short reduces p99 tail for small queries by 9ms while saving ~6% cost.
- Quant fallback latency overhead measured: median +6ms lookup + negligible routing overhead. Fallback to int4 on compatible HW reduced cost by additional 22% at similar quality in our internal evals (prompt set A/B).
- Rollback path: presets are namespaced by deployment tier, and the router respects tenant overrides. We added a feature toggle runtime.flag.econ.mosaic.enabled which is off by default and will be enabled during staged rollout.

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests: runtime/config/presets tests + adapter selection tree covering all fallback branches.
- Integration: perf-canary scenarios added under benchmark-lab that replay three canonical workloads for 2 hours each to validate cold-start and steady-state behaviour.
- Evals: ran small-scale quality eval to compare quant fallback variants; no statistically significant degradation seen on conversational BLEU/ROUGE proxies for the sampled prompts used by ENG-6112.

Deployment plan:
1) Merge to main behind flag
2) Canary enable in perf-canary and one internal tenant (10%) for 48h, run full telem/alerts
3) If stable, gradually increase to 50% over 7 days; then transition to 100% for cost-optimized tiers while staying opt-in for strict low-latency tenants
4) Post-rollout audit: run Optimize regressions to ensure no accidental quality regressions

Backward compatibility: All existing tenant configs are respected. Default behavior only changes for tenants without explicit batching/quantization overrides. No model schema breaking changes.

Related work: ENG-6127 (automated profile recommendations), ENG-6112 (unit-econ telemetry foundations). See also SUP-1983 incident notes for customer who experienced cost spikes when fallback quant variants were unavailable.

Notes for reviewers: pay attention to the adapter compatibility matrix (runtime/router/quant_compat.yaml) and the telemetry privacy constraints. The migration script is idempotent but runs slow on large catalogs; we run it as a background job in the migration path.

review_conversation: Marco Alvarez (reviewer): Can the compatibility matrix be expanded to include older CUDA major versions? Response: We already limit fallbacks to hardware reported via device_capabilities; adding explicit CUDA mapping would duplicate logic and become stale. Instead we added a short test in quant_adapter_test.go that verifies behavior on simulated older capabilities.

Samantha Li (reviewer): Are the telemetry fields PII-safe? Response: yes — we only emit aggregated counters and hashed model ids; added unit tests that assert no raw prompt or user identifiers are included.
Akash Mehta (approver): LGTM after io safety nit. Author: fixed the file handle leak in router and added test verifying no fd leaks under repeated routing.

QA (comment): Canary run initial 24h looked stable; one tenant reported minor cold-start latency spike on assistant.long, investigating warmup heuristics. Author: adjusted prefill threshold in assistant.long preset to reduce cold-start delay.
release_notes: Introduce 'mosaic' default presets (conv.default, assistant.long, search.short, rerank.tight) to improve unit economics by selecting workload-aware batching and KV cache defaults; add quant-fallback-adapter to transparently route to compatible quantized variants when requested profiles are unavailable or budget-constrained. Rollout behind runtime flag; safe canary planned.
notes_for_release_manager: Enable runtime.flag.econ.mosaic.enabled only in perf-canary and then follow staged rollout. Migration script located at model-catalog/migrations/2026-02-add-mosaic-hints.go must be queued as a background job; estimate runtime for current catalog: ~24h.
